summary: Saint Lucia is visa-free for citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, China and most Commonwealth countries. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens get up to six weeks, which the Immigration Department can extend, and Saint Lucia publishes no figure for other passports; CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. About fifty nationalities, many in Africa and Asia including India, need a visa that is issued at the port of entry, and the rest need a visa arranged through a Saint Lucian mission before traveling.

tips.text: Unless you hold an EU passport (90 days in any 180 under the EU agreement), expect an initial stay that may be as short as six weeks rather than the 90 days visitors expect elsewhere in the Caribbean. Check the date the officer writes in your passport, and apply to the Immigration Department in Castries before it expires if you plan to stay longer.
The UK government says it is illegal for anyone in Saint Lucia, including children, to dress in camouflage clothing. Pack something else.
Traffic drives on the left, according to Canada's travel advice, and the UK government says visitors without a Saint Lucian driving licence must get a temporary driving permit.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, China and most Commonwealth countries enter visa-free, and CARICOM nationals get six months. About fifty nationalities, including India, Kenya, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, need a visa that the Department of External Affairs lists as issued at the port of entry. Other nationalities must obtain a visa from a Saint Lucian mission or honorary consulate before traveling. There is no eVisa.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Lucia without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Saint Lucia waiver agreement, and Saint Lucia’s visa list gives Norwegians and Swiss the same. The UK and Canadian governments say their citizens are admitted for up to six weeks. For other visa-free passports Saint Lucia publishes no figure. The exact period is written on your stamp and is often matched to your onward ticket, so check it before leaving the airport; the Immigration Department in Castries can extend it.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes — the online Embarkation/Disembarkation (ED) form, which replaced the paper immigration and customs card in 2022. Complete it no more than 72 hours before you travel, one per family or group, and show the emailed receipt with your passport at immigration.

faq.question: Is camouflage clothing really banned in Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says it is illegal for anyone, including children, to dress in camouflage clothing in Saint Lucia, so leave camouflage-pattern clothes and bags at home.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from or transiting a country with risk of yellow fever transmission in tropical Africa or South America. Travelers from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean are not asked for one.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply in Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes. Saint Lucia is a CARICOM and OECS member, so nationals of member states receive a definite entry of up to six months on arrival, without a visa.
